summary.whatChanges: The CSRF middleware now treats OPTIONS as a safe HTTP method alongside GET and HEAD, so OPTIONS requests skip origin/Sec-Fetch-Site validation and pass through to the handler instead of being rejected. A test asserts OPTIONS /form returns 200.
behaviorChanges: OPTIONS requests are no longer blocked by the CSRF middleware regardless of Origin header
Cross-origin preflight OPTIONS requests reach the route handler and return its response (e.g. 200 OK) instead of a CSRF failure
risks: Applications that defined state-changing logic on OPTIONS routes lose CSRF protection for those routes
Behavior change is silent — existing deployments relying on OPTIONS being rejected will now allow those requests through
